summary: The note rounds up Premier League action on 23 December 2023. West Ham beat Manchester United through goals from Jarrod Bowen and Mohammed Kudus, increasing pressure on Erik ten Hag, while Arsenal drew 1-1 at Liverpool to top the table at Christmas. Tottenham beat Everton 2-1 under Ange Postecoglou, and Luton, Burnley and Bournemouth also won.
one_line: West Ham hammer Manchester United as ten Hag faces pressure, Arsenal draw at Liverpool, and Spurs beat Everton in the Premier League.
key_facts: Jarrod Bowen bundled home in the 72nd minute for West Ham, his 11th league goal this season, and Mohammed Kudus then scored his fourth goal in as many games.
Manchester United suffered a 13th defeat in 26 games in all competitions under Erik ten Hag.
Peter Schmeichel said of United: "There was no plan to it" and that he did not know the team's identity or style of play; he noted four games without a goal.
Erik ten Hag told the BBC it was "a decent 72 minutes where we didn't take our chances" before "one moment of switching off".
Liverpool and Arsenal drew 1-1 at Anfield, which ensures Arsenal top the Premier League on Christmas Day, a point clear of Liverpool and third-placed Aston Villa.

Gabriel headed Arsenal in front in the fourth minute from Martin Odegaard's free kick, the Gunners' fastest ever goal at Anfield in Premier League history; Mohamed Salah levelled in the 29th minute, beating David Raya at his near post.
Liverpool hit the woodwork twice in the second half, through Trent Alexander-Arnold and substitute Harvey Elliott.
Liverpool defender Kostas Tsimikas broke his collarbone after stumbling into Jurgen Klopp, who fell on top of him; Klopp said he will be "out for a long time."
Andros Townsend headed the winner for Luton Town against Newcastle United, their first match since captain Tom Lockyer suffered a cardiac arrest against Bournemouth a week earlier.

Richarlison scored for a third consecutive match against his old club Everton as Tottenham won 2-1 at home; Son Heung-min added a goal and Andre Gomes scored a late consolation for Everton, and Spurs will be in the top four at Christmas.
A Dominic Calvert-Lewin effort for Everton was ruled out by VAR in the 51st minute.
Burnley beat Fulham 2-0 through Wilson Odobert and Sander Berge, lifting them off the bottom, as Rebecca Welch became the first female referee to take charge of an EPL match.

Dominic Solanke scored a hat-trick, the winner a header in the fifth minute of stoppage time, as Bournemouth beat Nottingham Forest 3-2 in Nuno Espirito Santo's first game in charge; Forest's Willy Boly was sent off in the first half.
